about: A candidate playbook for ab-run (deck@variant) and runner/ab.py --data: the shipped version 1 with answer rules (wipes, Elspeth's and Chandra's sweeping loyalty abilities, Gideon's +2, the attack deterrents). Only the playbook object is read; the deck's data stays in its own file.

rules.ability: Destroy all artifacts, creatures, and enchantments
Destroy all creatures with power 4 or greater
Remove a loyalty counter from each
At the beginning of your upkeep, this emblem deals 1 damage

playbook.notes:
Version 2 (candidate, not shipped): version 1's rules unchanged and in their order, with answer rules added, written from the 200 games of this seat in league-run #3 (seed 20261250, every seat a bot), where the deck won 29 and Forge's attack sent 15.4 attackers a game at its planeswalkers (walkers left the battlefield for the graveyard 1,029 times in the 171 games it did not win). League figures below are games drawn / cast from hand / in hand at the seat's last turn in a game it did not win. The deck's planeswalkers are all legendary and none is a creature on our side of a wipe, so every wipe in it is close to one-sided for this seat: what it costs us is tokens, mana rocks and the odd creature. At the top, before the turn's other plays, so the board is cleared before new tokens and walkers go down: (1) Urza's Ruinous Blast when an opponent has 4 or more creatures and more power than ours, or (2) can attack us for 12 or more and has more power (47/6/31: Forge's AI almost never casts it; it exiles every nonlegendary nonland permanent and leaves our walkers, Guff, Mangara, Kazuul and the Oaths); (3) Blasphemous Act on the same board as (1) (61/38/10; Forge casts it, the rule makes it sure and early); (4) Nevinyrral's Disk's activation on that board (53 drawn, 19 cast, 11 activations; it spares planeswalkers); (5) Chandra, Awakened Inferno's -3 (3 damage to each non-Elemental creature) when an opponent has 4 or more creatures and more creatures than we do: never used in the league, Forge took her +2 all 145 times; (6) Elspeth's -3 (destroy each creature with power 4 or more) when one opponent can attack us for 12 or more with 3 creatures or fewer, which means at least one of them has power 4 or more, and has more power than ours: never used in the league (113 +1, 10 -7); (7) Promise of Loyalty when an opponent has 4 or more creatures and more power and we have 2 creatures or fewer (74/24/39; version 1's hold until opp_power > power stays, this makes it cast). After the mana rocks, the deterrents to attacks on the walkers: Onakke Oathkeeper at once (57/39/15: a tax of 1 for each creature attacking a walker), Norn's Annex when an opponent has 3 or more creatures (55/29/22), Silent Arbiter on the board of (1) (47/14/17; version 1's hold stays and this rule casts it), Nevinyrral's Disk when an opponent has 3 or more creatures, so it is on the battlefield and untapped by the time (4) wants it. The last list of creatures gains Wall of Denial (49/21/26), Fog Bank (57/43/11), Norn's Annex and the Disk, so they are cast with mana left over whatever the board. Thresholds: 4 creatures is Hail, Caesar's for its one-sided wipe; 12 as a threat is the same as its Ruinous Ultimatum rule; neither was tuned on these games. Left to Forge as before: Path to Exile (57/55/1) and Swords to Plowshares (64/60/3), which it already casts; the single-target loyalty removal (Chandra, Torch -3 64 times, The Wanderer -2 65, Nahiri -2 70, Vronos -2 80). Not expressible: Guff Rewrites History (46 drawn, never cast, 33 in hand at a loss: it needs a target of every player's, which Forge's logic never agrees to) and Semester's End (an instant that saves walkers from attack or removal, wanted on another player's turn).
 Tried and dropped: Gideon Jura's +2 (an opponent's creatures must attack Gideon) when one opponent could attack for 8: it never fired in 8 local tables with Gideon out on 8 turns; the ability targets an opponent, so a rule needs Forge's logic to agree, and Forge's logic for that delayed trigger does not (the card is AI:RemoveDeck:All, its script notes the missing AI). Checked at 16 local tables of bots (seeds 20263040 and 20263041, opponents from bots-v2 under their playbooks; games read in the event log, not playbook_stats): every new rule but the Disk's play rule fired as meant at least once; the wipes took 1 to 9 of our permanents against 4 to 44 of the opponents' (Ruinous Blast 44 against 7 and 26 against 5; Chandra's -3 nine opponent creatures against two of ours). Win rate not measured: 3 wins of 16 is too few games to mean anything.
